severities.name: Debug
severities.meaning: Detail for investigations; emitted only with `DiagnosticsBuilder.debug` on.

events.name: Started
events.meaning: The node started with `profile` and `preset`.
events.cause: the app called `MeshLink.start` on a stopped node.
events.fix: none needed.

events.name: Stopped
events.meaning: The node stopped for `reason`.
events.cause: the app called `MeshLink.stop` or `MeshLink.resetIdentity` on a started node.
events.fix: none needed.

values.name: Requested
values.meaning: The app called `MeshLink.stop`.

values.name: IdentityReset
values.meaning: The app called `MeshLink.resetIdentity`.

events.name: UnsecuredProfile
events.meaning: The node started in `SecurityProfile.Unsecured`, on every start: anyone in radio range can read, forge and replay its traffic.
events.cause: the configuration chose `SecurityProfile.Unsecured`.
events.fix: choose `SecurityProfile.Classical` or `SecurityProfile.PostQuantum` unless every payload is public anyway.

events.name: OwnCertificateRenewed
events.meaning: The node renewed its certificate and static keys, as it does every 12 h (spec "Static-key rotation"); a message sealed to its earlier certificate still opens until that certificate expires.
events.cause: the rotation interval passed.
events.fix: none needed.

events.name: ScanWindow
events.meaning: A scan window started or stopped, as `phase` tells. A central scans in windows of 4 s and rests between them as long as its density class and `MeshLinkConfig.power` set; every window starts a fresh scan.
events.cause: the node scans as central.
events.fix: none needed.

fields.name: phase
fields.meaning: Whether the window started or stopped.

values.name: Started
values.meaning: The window started: the node scans.

values.name: Stopped
values.meaning: The window stopped: the node rests.

events.name: ScanFailed
events.meaning: The platform refused or stopped a scan, so the node stopped discovery; `platformCode` is Android's scan error or iOS's `CBError` code, if the platform gave one.
events.cause: Bluetooth turned off, the app lacks scan permission, or the platform ran out of scanners; Android error 2 also reports `ML8001`.
events.fix: check that Bluetooth is on and the app holds its permissions, then call `MeshLink.start` again.

fields.name: platformCode
fields.meaning: The platform's error code, or `null` if it gave none.

events.name: StaleAddressMarked
events.meaning: An address sighted without an advertisement, as a backgrounded iPhone advertises, failed vetting: the node couldn't connect to it or read its capability record, or the record's advertisement belongs to no peer of this mesh. Its sightings add no candidate until it goes unseen for 10 min.
events.cause: a phone of another mesh or app nearby, or a MeshLink peer that moved out of range during the dial.
events.fix: none needed. If a peer of this mesh stays unfound, check that both use the same mesh ID and security profile.

events.name: DensityClassChanged
events.meaning: The node's density class switched `from` one class `to` another, which sets its link budget and scan schedule. Each start begins in `DensityClass.Low`; a pinned class never switches.
events.cause: more or fewer peers in range than before.
events.fix: none needed. If the class flaps in a stable crowd, pin it with `Density.Pinned`.

events.name: AdvertisingFailed
events.meaning: The platform refused or stopped advertising, so centrals can't find the node for the rest of the run, as `CentralOnlyReason.AdvertisingFailed` shows; `platformCode` is Android's advertise error or iOS's `CBError` code, if the platform gave one. The node still scans and links as central.
events.cause: the platform ran out of advertisers, or another app holds them; Android error 1 means the advertisement is too large, a MeshLink defect.
events.fix: close other Bluetooth apps, then call `MeshLink.start` again.

fields.name: platformCode
fields.meaning: The platform's error code, or `null` if it gave none.

events.name: GattServiceFailed
events.meaning: The platform failed to publish the GATT service that serves the capability record, so the node stopped discovery; `platformCode` is Android's GATT status or iOS's `CBError` code, if the platform gave one.
events.cause: Bluetooth turned off, or the platform's GATT server failed.
events.fix: turn Bluetooth off and on, then call `MeshLink.start` again.

fields.name: platformCode
fields.meaning: The platform's error code, or `null` if it gave none.

events.name: LinkOpened
events.meaning: A link to `peer` opened as `role`, with an ATT MTU of `mtu` bytes: the hellos or the handshake completed, and the peer is listed in `MeshLink.peers`.
events.cause: a peer in range linked.
events.fix: none needed.

fields.name: role
fields.meaning: This node's role on the link.

fields.name: mtu
fields.meaning: The negotiated ATT MTU in bytes; each GATT write carries at most `mtu - 3` bytes.

values.name: Central

events.name: LinkClosed
events.meaning: An open link to `peer` closed for `reason`; `byPeer` tells whether the peer closed it. A link that closes before it opens reports why as `ML3003`, `ML3008` or `ML4001` instead.
events.cause: `Reason.Normal` or `Reason.ShuttingDown`: a node stopped. `Reason.DuplicateLink`: the two nodes linked both ways and kept one link. `Reason.ResourceLimit`: the closing node holds its link budget. `Reason.ProtocolError`: an incompatible or faulty peer, or a corrupted record. `Reason.ConnectionLost`: the peer moved out of range or its radio failed.
events.fix: none needed for a stop, a duplicate or a lost connection; the node links again when the peer is back. If `Reason.ProtocolError` repeats, update both apps to the same MeshLink version.

fields.name: byPeer
fields.meaning: Whether the peer closed the link; `false` if this node did or the connection was lost.

fields.name: platformCode
fields.meaning: For `Reason.ConnectionLost`, the platform's status: Android's GATT status, such as 8 for a supervision timeout, or iOS's `CBError` code; otherwise, or if the platform gave none, `null`.

events.name: ConnectFailed
events.meaning: A connect as central on `link` failed for `reason`. `attempt` counts from 1; a `Reason.Transient` failure is retried up to 3 times (spec `connect-retries`).
events.cause: the peer moved out of range or stopped advertising, or the platform failed the connect; Android reports GATT status 133 or 147 as `Reason.Transient`, often on a first connect.
events.fix: transient failures retry by themselves. If every connect fails, move the phones closer and turn Bluetooth off and on.

fields.name: link
fields.meaning: The link the connect was for.

fields.name: platformCode
fields.meaning: The platform's status: Android's GATT status, such as 133, or the `CBError` code of iOS's `didFailToConnect`; `null` if the platform gave none.

values.name: InvalidArgument

values.name: PeerUnreachable
values.meaning: The peer is out of range or no longer advertising.

values.name: CapabilityMissing

values.name: LinkClosed

values.name: Unsupported

values.name: RadioError

values.name: Transient

events.name: LinkCapReached
events.meaning: The node refused a bearer, as it holds `cap` links: its link budget, or the radio's cap on links as peripheral.
events.cause: many peers in range; expected in a dense mesh.
events.fix: none needed; the node links to other peers as its links close.

events.name: BearerFallback
events.meaning: An L2CAP CoC channel to `peer` failed to open for `reason`, so the link stays on GATT (spec "Bearer switch").
events.cause: the platform or the peer refused the channel.
events.fix: none needed; GATT carries the same traffic more slowly. If it happens with every peer, turn `MeshLinkConfigBuilder.l2capUpgrade` off.

fields.name: reason
fields.meaning: Why the channel failed to open.

values.name: InvalidArgument

values.name: PeerUnreachable

values.name: RadioError

events.name: GattOperationRetried
events.meaning: An Android GATT request found the stack busy and is being retried, every 10 ms for up to 1 s; reported once per request. `platformCode` is the busy status, 201, on Android 13 and later; older Android gives none.
events.cause: another app or the stack itself holds the phone's GATT queue.
events.fix: none needed unless it repeats; then close other Bluetooth apps on the phone.

fields.name: platformCode
fields.meaning: The platform's busy status, or `null` if it gave none.

events.name: UnknownLinkFrameDropped
events.meaning: An open link dropped a link-local frame of `type` it doesn't handle: an unknown type, or a `REKEY` on an `Unsecured` link. The link stays open.
events.cause: the peer runs a newer MeshLink version, or is faulty.
events.fix: none needed. If it repeats, update both apps to the same MeshLink version.

events.name: ProtocolVersionRejected
events.meaning: A link closed with no protocol version in common: the peer offered at most `theirVersion`.
events.cause: the peer runs a MeshLink version with an incompatible protocol.
events.fix: update both apps to the same MeshLink version.

fields.name: theirVersion
fields.meaning: The highest protocol version the peer offered.

events.name: BusyReply
events.meaning: A node refused a fragmented frame with `BUSY` for `reason`; `direction` tells which node. The link stays open, and the sender retries the message later (spec "Busy reply").
events.cause: `Reason.Slots`: the link reassembles its maximum number of frames, or its one large frame. `Reason.Budget`: the refusing node reassembles as many large frames as it can hold.
events.fix: none needed. If it repeats, send fewer large messages at once.

fields.name: direction
fields.meaning: Whether this node sent the `BUSY` or received it.

values.name: Received

values.meaning: The link reassembles its maximum number of frames, or its one large frame.

values.name: Budget
values.meaning: The refusing node's budget for large frames is spent.

events.name: BearerSwitched
events.meaning: The link to `peer` moved from GATT to an L2CAP CoC channel (spec "Bearer switch").
events.cause: both nodes support L2CAP CoC and have `MeshLinkConfig.l2capUpgrade` on.
events.fix: none needed.

events.name: HandshakeFailed
events.meaning: The handshake on `link` failed for `reason`, and the link closed.
events.cause: `Reason.Timeout`: the peer moved away or is overloaded. `Reason.Decrypt`: the peer uses another security profile, mesh ID or mesh key. `Reason.Certificate`: the peer's certificate is invalid or expired, often a wrong clock. `Reason.Protocol`: an incompatible or faulty peer.
events.fix: give every phone of the mesh the same security profile, mesh ID and mesh key, and a correct clock.

values.name: Timeout
values.meaning: Not complete within `handshake-timeout` after the bearer opened.

values.name: Decrypt
values.meaning: A handshake message failed to decrypt or carried an unusable key. Another security profile, mesh ID or mesh key all fail this way.

values.name: Certificate
values.meaning: The peer's certificate was missing, invalid, expired, or bound another key.

values.name: Protocol
values.meaning: An unexpected, malformed or version-changing handshake frame.

events.name: HandshakeLimitDropped
events.meaning: A handshake broke a denial-of-service bound, `limit`, so the bearer closed without a reply (spec "Handshake limits").
events.cause: many phones connecting at once, or a peer opening handshakes faster than allowed.
events.fix: none needed; honest peers succeed on a later attempt.

values.name: PerBearer
values.meaning: A second handshake on one bearer (`handshake-half-open-per-link`).

values.name: Global
values.meaning: More than `handshake-half-open-global` handshakes at once.

values.name: NeighborInterval
values.meaning: A new handshake from one address within `handshake-neighbor-interval`.

events.name: BroadcastSignatureInvalid
events.meaning: A signed broadcast reached the node whose signature did not verify, so the node neither delivered nor relayed it (spec "BROADCAST").
events.cause: a faulty or malicious peer, or bytes corrupted in transit.
events.fix: none needed; if it repeats, look for a peer that forges broadcasts.

events.name: RouteFound
events.meaning: Route discovery found a route to `peer`, `hops` hops away, so `MeshLink.peers` lists it as `Reachability.Routed`.
events.cause: the node sent to or heard from a peer beyond its links.
events.fix: none needed.

fields.name: peer
fields.meaning: The peer the route leads to.

events.name: RouteLost
events.meaning: `MeshLink.peers` no longer lists `peer` as `Reachability.Routed`: its route expired, or the key its routing tags derive from lapsed.
events.cause: the peer moved away or stopped, or no message used its route.
events.fix: none needed; the next message to the peer searches for a route anew.

fields.name: peer
fields.meaning: The peer the route led to.

events.name: UnknownRoutedFrameRelayed
events.meaning: The node relayed a routed frame of `type`, a type this version does not know, by its header alone (spec "Unicast forwarding", "Flood forwarding").
events.cause: a peer runs a newer version of MeshLink.
events.fix: none needed; update the app to use the newer type.

events.name: ExpiryFarFromLocalTime
events.meaning: The node dropped a routed frame whose expiry lies outside what its clock accepts (spec "Routing headers"): the sender's clock and this phone's differ by at least `skewSeconds`, positive if the sender's runs ahead, negative if it runs behind.
events.cause: a phone whose clock is set by hand, or wrong.
events.fix: set every phone of the mesh to the network-provided time.

fields.name: skewSeconds
fields.meaning: The least the clocks differ by, in seconds.

events.name: HeldMessageEvicted
events.meaning: The node gave up a frame it held for others to make room for a new one (spec "Holding"), for `reason`.
events.cause: `Reason.LinkShare`: one link sent more than its share of the frames held. `Reason.ClosestToExpiry`: the hold is full and no link is over its share.
events.fix: none needed. If it repeats, peers that come back later may miss messages; send fewer messages to absent peers.

values.name: LinkShare
values.meaning: It came from a link over its share of the hold; that link's frame closest to expiry gave way.

values.name: ClosestToExpiry
values.meaning: The hold is full and no link is over its share; the frame closest to expiry gave way.

events.name: CertificateLookup
events.meaning: A certificate lookup brought `peer`'s certificate after `attempts` requests (spec "Certificate lookup"), so the node can seal messages to it.
events.cause: the node sent to a peer it has never linked with.
events.fix: none needed.

events.name: CertificateLookupUnanswered
events.meaning: The lookup of `peer`'s certificate got no valid reply by its deadline, after `attempts` requests (spec "Certificate lookup"). A message that waited for it was never sealed to `peer`.
events.cause: the peer is out of reach of the mesh, or stopped.
events.fix: bring the phones closer together, or send again once the peer is listed in `MeshLink.peers`.

events.name: InvalidCertificateReply
events.meaning: A reply to this node's certificate lookup failed to open, or held no valid certificate of the peer looked up (spec "Certificate lookup"). The node drops it and waits for another.
events.cause: a faulty or hostile node answered, or the peer's certificate has expired.
events.fix: none needed if a valid reply follows; otherwise check the peer's clock.

events.name: DiagnosticsDropped
events.meaning: This collector fell `dropped` events behind, so its oldest events were dropped. Each collector buffers 256 events.
events.cause: the collector does slow work for each event.
events.fix: collect on a fast path and move slow work elsewhere.

fields.name: dropped
fields.meaning: How many events this collector lost.

events.name: ReadTrackingEvicted
events.meaning: The oldest delivered message awaiting a read receipt was forgotten, as more than 1,000 were tracked; its status stays `DeliveryStatus.Delivered`.
events.cause: the app sends many messages that request read receipts, and their recipients don't read them.
events.fix: request read receipts only for messages whose reading matters.

fields.name: messageId
fields.meaning: A copy of the forgotten message's `message_id`.

events.name: InboxFull
events.meaning: A received message was dropped because the messages waiting for the app reached `bound` (ADR 0007 decision 9). Its sender gets no delivery receipt and retries.
events.cause: the app does not collect `MeshLink.messages`, or collects it slowly.
events.fix: collect `MeshLink.messages` for as long as the node runs.

fields.name: bound
fields.meaning: The bound the message would have crossed.

values.name: Count
values.meaning: At most 1,024 messages wait.

values.name: Bytes
values.meaning: At most 1 MiB of payload waits.

values.name: Sender
values.meaning: One sender's messages hold at most a quarter of the payload bytes.

events.name: ReassemblyBudgetExhausted
events.meaning: This node refused a large fragmented frame with `BUSY`, as the frames it reassembles hold its budget of 512 KiB for large frames across links.
events.cause: several peers send large messages through this node at once.
events.fix: none needed; the senders retry later. If it repeats, send fewer large messages at once.

events.name: ScannerRegistrationFailed
events.meaning: Android refused a scan with error 2, `SCAN_FAILED_APPLICATION_REGISTRATION_FAILED`: the Bluetooth stack holds scanner registrations an earlier process leaked. Reported beside `ML2002`.
events.cause: an app, often this one after a crash, leaked scanner registrations.
events.fix: turn Bluetooth off and on; if that fails, restart the phone.
